newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Alcohol available in NZ falls in September yr - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: Alcohol available in NZ falls in September yr - SNZ.

text.p: The amount of alcohol available per person aged 15 years and over in New Zealand fell by 4.3 percent in the year to September compared with the same period in 1995, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday.
This was the seventh consecutive September year to record a decrease.

The total volume of alcoholic beverage available had also declined. In the September year 404.8 million litres of alcoholic beverage was available for consumption, 3.9 percent or 16.3 million litres less than in the September 1995 year.

Wine was the only beverage to record an increase in availability. The total volume of wine available increased by 3.0 percent in the year to September. The volume of table wine increased 2.8 percent, while the volume of fortified wine available recorded the highest increase of 6.5 percent.
The total volume of beer available fell by 5.0 percent or 17.5 million litres.

The only type of beer to increase in availability in the year was beer with an alcohol content between 4.36 percent and 5.0 percent. This rose by 12.7 percent compared with the previous September year.
The total volume of spirits decreased by 5.7 percent reaching a level of 9.2 million litres. This was a decrease of 0.6 million litres over the September 1995 year.
